page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by KVM virtualization. The configuration provides 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs via a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache. System memory totals 48.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512 with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), AES, BMI2, and FMA.

Network connectivity features an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external block storage for persistent filesystem needs, and contains zero GPUs. Performance benchmarks show middle-tier results for parallel execution, including a PassMark CPU score of 21,643.62, Geekbench multi-core score of 8,967.0, and stress-ng multi-core output of 21,007.3. Memory throughput tests show 108.94 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 47.99 GB/sec on writes. However, single-core processing capabilities are constrained, as indicated by bottom-quartile ratings in single-threaded gzip compression and stress-ng single-core tests.

With its 24 dedicated virtual cores and moderate per-core memory footprint, the instance offers predictable multi-threaded computing capability without the fluctuations of burstable platforms. The tradeoff lies between competent parallel performance and lower per-thread single-core speeds. The hardware profile is best aligned with multi-threaded application tiers, continuous integration and build servers, static web serving clusters, and distributed batch processing pipelines.

It delivers 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores alongside 48.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and FMA instructions. Networking provides an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while the instance includes no bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields average multi-core throughput across PassMark, Geekbench, and stress-ng suites, though single-core execution metrics such as single-threaded compression fall into lower percentiles. The absence of attached local storage necessitates network storage volumes for stateful operations. This instance fits multi-threaded computation, continuous integration builds, distributed batch processing, and mid-tier web application serving where parallel CPU density is prioritized over massive per-core memory.
